title: fix(update): ride out state database contention instead of failing the update
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Updates must not abort because an optional progress receipt encounters a busy shared-state writer. This addresses the `updater-runtime-retention` incident in #168072. Thanks @jlapenna for the incident evidence.

The latest CI failure exposed a production classification bug: main retained additional timing steps for diagnostic history, while this PR used that retention list to decide which writes recovery requires. Retaining a timer accidentally made its write fatal under contention.

## User Impact

The update CLI explicitly allows required worker-backed writes up to 120 seconds for SQLite writer admission. Gateway-side callers keep their ordinary five-second budget. Optional progress and timing writes use a one-second budget, then warn and continue without claiming a committed receipt.

Recovery-critical phase, ownership, rollback, and failure receipts remain required. History eviction priority now has no effect on that decision. No schema, config, environment, CLI option, or dependency change is authored by this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

`isRequiredUpdateRunStep` now owns an explicit recovery policy rather than borrowing `isRetainedStep` from bounded-history compaction. The recovery policy keeps phase transitions, finalization, driver identity, notice custody, reconciliation, database recovery diagnostics, rollback, and failed/signaled receipts. Timing-only retention, candidate, and handoff observations remain best effort.

The long budget is opt-in from the update driver's existing asynchronous writer path. SQLite owns native busy retries; no transaction is held while an application retry loop waits, and admitted mutations are not replayed. Mutation and commit restore the ordinary five-second budget. The separate Doctor fix invalidates the parent's schema admission after its child settles, using the child's effective state path.

The exact failing CI merge base (`c3fcd1554c3405c942bc03ec85fcbac8a0bb12a3`) was integrated normally, without rewriting history, so local proof includes main's new retained timing keys. The production fix is independent of platform timing.

## Evidence

Revision head: `7a069cbfa2785c001eef280c75228a676b4b2243`.

- [CI run 38068510314, job 114261240504](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38068510314/job/114261240504) tested merge `8cd4441af05756932b1d42125768e9941f3868b3`, combining this branch with the base above. Main commit `5c63a7867a80` (#168409) added `updater-runtime-retention` and its diagnostic row to compaction retention. That made the old recovery predicate classify them as required. The unmerged branch passed standalone Linux; the actual merge policy reproduced the failure. Earlier macOS repetition was not proof against that merge.
- Linux negative control on the integrated base: **6 failed / 8 passed**. Four retained-timing policy cases, the synchronous warning case, and the real SQLite lock case failed before the production predicate fix. The native error was `ERR_SQLITE_ERROR`, `errcode: 5`, correctly recognized as contention; it was the required/bookkeeping decision that was wrong.
- Final **Linux Docker: 10/10 file runs, 14/14 tests each**. Image `node:24`, digest `sha256:3d27e5c11e5786e309ec3e03f93ae536eb36e6e5eb3714d5eb3300a36157add0`; Node 24.21.0, Linux ARM64, SQLite 3.53.4. The worktree was mounted read-only and copied to a private volume; HOME and state were isolated. Command: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-run-contention.test.ts`. Per-run wall time 14–21s; measured test time 5.489–6.257s (median 5.920s). Committed production/test hashes exactly match the tested copies.
- The replacement suite injects native-shaped `SQLITE_BUSY` failures to test policy directly, verifies no receipt or transaction admission is claimed, and checks warning/continued terminal-outcome behavior. Required writes preserve the driver's native busy budget and can succeed on a subsequent attempt. One real SQLite case keeps a competing transaction open with a **zero** busy timeout; there are no sleeps, global clocks, or timed-release simulations. The former simulated 107-second test is removed and is not claimed as current proof.
- Direct production importers and ledger/diagnostic siblings: **9 files, 114 tests passed**, 166.13s wrapper wall. `madge`: zero import cycles. `check-changed` passed its initial guards, core typecheck, and all 27 test type graphs. It remains non-green for inherited base issues: UI test roots 722 exceed 720 in `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json`; unused `default` in `tools/solid-lint/index.mjs`; unused `resolveSessionConversationStub` / `resolveSessionTargetStub` in `src/agents/tools/sessions-channel-fixture.test-support.ts`. Those files match the integrated base. Core lint initially caught three missing braces in the rewritten test; they were fixed, both changed files then passed the same typed core lint configuration, and the exact final test file passed the ten Linux runs above. Remaining ownership/cycle/script guards passed; no baseline was altered.
- Earlier requester regression proof remains relevant to unchanged Doctor code: the exact migrated requester case failed on main hourly run `38032195500`; invalidating parent admission repaired it, and ten local Linux requester runs passed with the original assertion. The shared command-transport mock and legacy-handoff fixture use their actual helper/writer owners; no assertions were weakened.
- Fresh independent read-only review found no actionable P1/P2 or omitted recovery consumer. Managed Codex review was attempted with isolation and returned timeout/HTTP 401 without a verdict.

Cumulative numstat against the integrated CI base: production **+151/-34 (+117 net)**; tests **+292/-7**; test support/routing/baseline **+40/-37**; docs **+9/-0**. Total **+492/-78** across 19 files. Hosted CI on this head is pending. No PR merge or live operator update is performed.
